page: Amazon Web Services m6a.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by third-generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with two threads per core running at 3.6 GHz. It is paired with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions, while AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets are absent. The configuration does not bundle local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators like GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage via a 38 Gbps baseline network interconnect.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute capabilities, led by a top-tier stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 143,441.36 and a PassMark encryption rating of 110,483.6. General multi-core benchmarks remain consistently in the top 25%, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 81,621.72, a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,877.0, and high-throughput compilation and ray tracing execution. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench single-core at 1,702.0 and text processing, place within the middle 50% tier, highlighting a configuration prioritized for high-density multi-threaded workloads rather than peak single-threaded execution speed.

Memory subsystem testing shows high cached performance, reaching 6,034.75 GB/sec on small-block read tests, while large uncached block reads scale down to 133.81 GB/sec. Application-level metrics remain competitive for distributed workloads, delivering 90.99 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database operation scores. Natural language processing on CPU exhibits robust throughput on smaller models (up to 2,896.15 prompt tokens per second on 135M architectures), though generation speeds moderate significantly on 7B and 70B parameter models. Without local NVMe storage, disk-heavy applications must account for network I/O overhead over the 38 Gbps network interface.

The m6a.24xlarge instance provides efficient core density and balanced resource scaling for multi-threaded enterprise workloads. It is functionally well-suited for high-concurrency backend services, large-scale software builds, enterprise database deployments, in-memory caching clusters, and mid-tier computational workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) based on the AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It includes 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance provides 38 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes no bundled local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its multi-core parallel compute and cryptographic throughput in the top tiers, reaching 143,441.36 on multi-core stress-ng tests and 90.99 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics and uncached memory bandwidth fall within average performance bands. Given its balanced resource footprint and strong multi-threading, it is well matched for enterprise application servers, memory caching layers, continuous integration build clusters, and transactional databases.
